first.rationale: Current situation shows both activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) declining simultaneously. Memory_31 and memory_86 both support simplification as a lever—memory_31 on SMB signup friction, memory_86 on completion rates. I'm verifying memory_31 (day 12, earliest) and memory_73 (day 31) because: (1) memory_31 is foundational to the simplification hypothesis but oldest and least recently validated; (2) memory_73 addresses competitor pricing pressure directly, and I need to confirm its specificity before deprioritizing promotional_pricing. Simplify_onboarding targets the measurable activation/completion decline with highest confidence from durable record, addresses both metrics simultaneously, and preserves optionality on pricing response (can layer in later if needed). Standard experiment scale matches weekly constraint and single-slot capacity.

final.rationale: Verification confirms memory_31 (signup simplification, +9% activation on SMB) is robust and directly addresses the -6% QoQ activation decline. Memory_73 archive reveals targeted promotional pricing acquired poor-quality cohorts with -12% retention and failed at renewal—this is unsustainable for long-term qualified revenue objective despite competitor pressure. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is also validated but simplification targets two simultaneous metrics (activation AND onboarding completion both declining). Enterprise_sales_assist would not address SMB activation deterioration. Referral_incentive (memory_57) requires healthy baseline activation to work. Simplify_onboarding is the highest-confidence lever: it directly repairs the measurable funnel decline, avoids the retention damage of discounting, and aligns with primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The -4% onboarding completion and -6% activation decline together suggest friction barriers, not pricing sensitivity—simplification is the right diagnosis.
